q-75333.name: Question 1
q-75333.problem:
Let $R=[-1,4]\times [3,6]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=4x+7y-16.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75333.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=4x+7y-16$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=4x+7y-16$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/67daa328cc6ae4cb37be386c327fb4548844fad2adc10476bdf1147c5a5d4218.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/6e58954fccd74eaf67c95df818c4c9050c35b324c5fffe4902a366cb295b8845.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j})=4{x}_{i}+7{y}_{j}-16\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(4{x}_{i}+7{y}_{j}-16)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $4{x}_{i}+7{y}_{j}-16.$

Question 1
?

Let R=[−1,4]×[3,6] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=4x+7y−16. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
−xi+4yj
b
4xi+7yj−1−16
c
4xi+7yj−16
d
4xi−1+7yj−1−16
e
−xi−1+4yj−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=4x+7y−16 increases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=4x+7y−16 increases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi,yj)=4xi+7yj−16 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(4xi+7yj−16)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 4xi+7yj−16.

q-75335.html:
Question 2
?

Let R=[3,4]×[1,9] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=3x2+8y2−21. Further, let P be a partition of R, where P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
3xi2+8yj2−21
b
3xi−12+8yj−12−21
c
3xi−12+4yj−12
d
3xi2+8yj−12−21
e
3xi2+4yj2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj

where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=3x2+8y2−21 increases as x increases on [3,4], and

  • f(x,y)=3x2+8y2−21 increases as y increases on [1,9].

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

Therefore, Mij=f(xi,yj)=3xi2+8yj2−21 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(3xi2+8yj2−21)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 3xi2+8yj2−21.

q-75330.name: Question 3
q-75330.problem:
Let $R=[-2,4]\times [-2,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=3x+4y+15.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75330.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=3x+4y+15$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=3x+4y+15$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/67daa328cc6ae4cb37be386c327fb4548844fad2adc10476bdf1147c5a5d4218.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/6e58954fccd74eaf67c95df818c4c9050c35b324c5fffe4902a366cb295b8845.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j})=3{x}_{i}+4{y}_{j}+15\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(3{x}_{i}+4{y}_{j}+15)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $3{x}_{i}+4{y}_{j}+15.$

q-75330.html:
Question 3
?

Let R=[−2,4]×[−2,2] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=3x+4y+15. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
−2xi+4yj
b
3xi+4yj+15
c
−2xi−1+4yj−1
d
3xi+4yj−1+15
e
3xi−1+4yj−1+15
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=3x+4y+15 increases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=3x+4y+15 increases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi,yj)=3xi+4yj+15 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is

U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(3xi+4yj+15)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 3xi+4yj+15.

q-75336.name: Question 4
q-75336.problem:
Let $R=[3,13]\times [3,7]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=12{x}^{2}+19{y}^{2}+3.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75336.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=12{x}^{2}+19{y}^{2}+3$ increases as $x$ increases on $[3,13],$ and

- $f(x,y)=12{x}^{2}+19{y}^{2}+3$ increases as $y$ increases on $[3,7].$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/67daa328cc6ae4cb37be386c327fb4548844fad2adc10476bdf1147c5a5d4218.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/6e58954fccd74eaf67c95df818c4c9050c35b324c5fffe4902a366cb295b8845.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j})=12{x}_{i}^{2}+19{y}_{j}^{2}+3\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(12{x}_{i}^{2}+19{y}_{j}^{2}+3)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $12{x}_{i}^{2}+19{y}_{j}^{2}+3.$

q-75336.html:
Question 4
?

Let R=[3,13]×[3,7] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=12x2+19y2+3. Further, let P be a partition of R, where P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
12xi−12+19yj−12+3
b
12xi2+19yj2+3
c
12xi2+19yj−12+3
d
3xi−12+13yj−12
e
3xi2+13yj2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=12x2+19y2+3 increases as x increases on [3,13], and

  • f(x,y)=12x2+19y2+3 increases as y increases on [3,7].

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

Therefore, Mij=f(xi,yj)=12xi2+19yj2+3 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(12xi2+19yj2+3)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 12xi2+19yj2+3.

q-170677.name: Question 5
q-170677.problem:
Let $R=[0,5]\times [1,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)={x}^{3}+3{y}^{2}.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-170677.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)={x}^{3}+3{y}^{2}$ increases as $x$ increases on $[0,5],$ and

- $f(x,y)={x}^{3}+3{y}^{2}$ increases as $y$ increases on $[1,2].$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/67daa328cc6ae4cb37be386c327fb4548844fad2adc10476bdf1147c5a5d4218.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/6e58954fccd74eaf67c95df818c4c9050c35b324c5fffe4902a366cb295b8845.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j})={x}_{i}^{3}+3{y}_{i}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i}^{3}+3{y}_{j}^{2})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is ${x}_{i}^{3}+3{y}_{j}^{2}.$

Let R=[0,5]×[1,2] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=x3+3y2. Further, let P be a partition of R, where P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

  • f(x,y)=x3+3y2 increases as x increases on [0,5], and

  • f(x,y)=x3+3y2 increases as y increases on [1,2].

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

q-75343.problem:
Let $R=[1,2]\times [0,1]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=30-7{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75343.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=30-7{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ decreases as $x$ increases on $[1,2],$ and

- $f(x,y)=30-7{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ decreases as $y$ increases on $[0,1].$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/ce0d90127e1f14654f4b32a933f1eb6e76e054c03f19ca40c3f04116aa3c2c93.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/5b9967c814e46914e0409854de0960e85339adc9b9fd9693677c8e048c342702.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})=30-7{x}_{i-1}^{2}-{y}_{j-1}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(30-7{x}_{i-1}^{2}-{y}_{j-1}^{2})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $30-7{x}_{i-1}^{2}-{y}_{j-1}^{2}.$

q-75341.html:
Question 7
?

Let R=[0,1]×[−21,−3] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=−23−13x−14y. Further, let P be a partition of R, where P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
−21xi−3yj
b
−23−13xi−14yj
c
−23−13xi−1−14yj−1
d
−21xi−1−3yj−1
e
−23−13xi−1−14yj
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by

U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj

where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=−23−13x−14y decreases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=−23−13x−14y decreases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the smallest possible y. This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi−1,yj−1)=−23−13xi−1−14yj−1 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(−23−13xi−1−14yj−1)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is −23−13xi−1−14yj−1.

q-170680.name: Question 8
q-170680.problem:
Let $R=[-2,2]\times [-1,1]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=-5x-4y-1.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-170680.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=-5x-4y-1$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=-5x-4y-1$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/ce0d90127e1f14654f4b32a933f1eb6e76e054c03f19ca40c3f04116aa3c2c93.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/5b9967c814e46914e0409854de0960e85339adc9b9fd9693677c8e048c342702.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})=-5{x}_{i-1}-4{y}_{j-1}-1\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(-5{x}_{i-1}-4{y}_{j-1}-1)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $-5{x}_{i-1}-4{y}_{j-1}-1.$

q-170680.html:
Question 8
?

Let R=[−2,2]×[−1,1] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=−5x−4y−1. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
−5xi−4yj−1
b
−10xi−1−8yj−1
c
−5xi−1−4yj−1−1
d
−10xi−8yj−1
e
−52xi−2yj
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by

U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj

where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=−5x−4y−1 decreases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=−5x−4y−1 decreases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the smallest possible y. This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi−1,yj−1)=−5xi−1−4yj−1−1 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is

U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(−5xi−1−4yj−1−1)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is −5xi−1−4yj−1−1.

q-75342.name: Question 9
q-75342.problem:
Let $R=[0,1]\times [0,1]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=15-3{x}^{2}-7{y}^{2}.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75342.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=15-3{x}^{2}-7{y}^{2}$ decreases as $x$ increases on $[0,1],$ and

- $f(x,y)=15-3{x}^{2}-7{y}^{2}$ decreases as $y$ increases on $[0,1].$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/ce0d90127e1f14654f4b32a933f1eb6e76e054c03f19ca40c3f04116aa3c2c93.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/5b9967c814e46914e0409854de0960e85339adc9b9fd9693677c8e048c342702.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})=15-3{x}_{i-1}^{2}-7{y}_{j-1}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(15-3{x}_{i-1}^{2}-7{y}_{j-1}^{2})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $15-3{x}_{i-1}^{2}-7{y}_{j-1}^{2}.$

q-75342.html:
Question 9
?

Let R=[0,1]×[0,1] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=15−3x2−7y2. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
xi−12+yj−12
b
15−3xi−12−7yj2
c
15−3xi−12−7yj−12
d
15−3xi2−7yj2
e
xi2+yj2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=15−3x2−7y2 decreases as x increases on [0,1], and

  • f(x,y)=15−3x2−7y2 decreases as y increases on [0,1].

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the smallest possible y. This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi−1,yj−1)=15−3xi−12−7yj−12 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(15−3xi−12−7yj−12)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 15−3xi−12−7yj−12.

q-75339.name: Question 10
q-75339.problem:
Let $R=[-5,2]\times [2,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=35-3x-9y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75339.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=35-3x-9y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=35-3x-9y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/ce0d90127e1f14654f4b32a933f1eb6e76e054c03f19ca40c3f04116aa3c2c93.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/5b9967c814e46914e0409854de0960e85339adc9b9fd9693677c8e048c342702.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})=35-3{x}_{i-1}-9{y}_{j-1}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(35-3{x}_{i-1}-9{y}_{j-1})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $35-3{x}_{i-1}-9{y}_{j-1}.$

q-75346.problem:
Let $R=[2,7]\times [-13,-5]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=4x-7y+8.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$
what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-75346.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=4x-7y+8$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=4x-7y+8$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/01b291ca7cd81b88cf6ed06fdcdb2ffcbb1f78255d0f57d496823d347c2fb0b3.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom right corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/de36b521dea1f925754a9c630c3d4a2c405c087a191138f1eaaa5771becb8c21.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j-1})=4{x}_{i}-7{y}_{j-1}+8\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(4{x}_{i}-7{y}_{j-1}+8)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $4{x}_{i}-7{y}_{j-1}+8.$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a

Notice that:

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible x and the smallest possible y. This is the value at the bottom right corner of each subregion.

$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-170684.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=8y-2x-5$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=8y-2x-5$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/ffa57d3e7fed08212f12d4b9d7c2e0a4d33a3aac71c8b8a03d1a9a7364484deb.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top left corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/74d546d91e145efea49b70af56cb472e8bbbd1417725cd7fa92a3a278cad75ea.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j})=8{y}_{j}-2{x}_{i-1}-5\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(8{y}_{j}-2{x}_{i-1}-5)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $8{y}_{j}-2{x}_{i-1}-5.$

q-170684.html:
Question 12
?

Let R=[−1,3]×[−4,−2] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=8y−2x−5. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj

where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
8yj−2xi−1−5
b
8yj−1−2xi−1−5
c
8yj−2xi−5
d
−2yj+3xi−5
e
−2yj−1−xi−1−5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=8y−2x−5 decreases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=8y−2x−5 increases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi−1,yj)=8yj−2xi−1−5 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(8yj−2xi−1−5)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 8yj−2xi−1−5.

q-123593.name: Question 13
q-123593.problem:
Let $R=[1,2]\times [2,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=y-x+5.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-123593.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=y-x+5$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=y-x+5$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/ffa57d3e7fed08212f12d4b9d7c2e0a4d33a3aac71c8b8a03d1a9a7364484deb.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top left corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/74d546d91e145efea49b70af56cb472e8bbbd1417725cd7fa92a3a278cad75ea.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j})={y}_{j}-{x}_{i-1}+5\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({y}_{j}-{x}_{i-1}+5)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is ${y}_{j}-{x}_{i-1}+5.$

q-123593.html:
Question 13
?

Let R=[1,2]×[2,3] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=y−x+5. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
yj−1−xi−1+5
b
2yj+xi−1
c
yj−xi+5
d
2yj−1+xi
e
yj−xi−1+5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=y−x+5 decreases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=y−x+5 increases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi−1,yj)=yj−xi−1+5 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(yj−xi−1+5)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is yj−xi−1+5.

q-122842.name: Question 14
q-122842.problem:
Let $R=[-3,2]\times [-5,-4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=4x-y+9.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$
what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
q-122842.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=4x-y+9$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=4x-y+9$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/01b291ca7cd81b88cf6ed06fdcdb2ffcbb1f78255d0f57d496823d347c2fb0b3.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom right corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/de36b521dea1f925754a9c630c3d4a2c405c087a191138f1eaaa5771becb8c21.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j-1})=4{x}_{i}-{y}_{j-1}+9\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(4{x}_{i}-{y}_{j-1}+9)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $4{x}_{i}-{y}_{j-1}+9.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/74d546d91e145efea49b70af56cb472e8bbbd1417725cd7fa92a3a278cad75ea.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j})=5{y}_{j}-3{x}_{i-1}+20\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(5{y}_{j}-3{x}_{i-1}+20)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $5{y}_{j}-3{x}_{i-1}+20.$

Question 15
?

Let R=[1,2]×[−1,1] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=5y−3x+20. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Given that the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj where Δxi=xi−xi−1 and Δyj=yj−yj−1, what is the missing expression in the double summation above?

a
5yj−3xi−1+20
b
5yj−1−3xi−1+20
c
2yj+xi−1
d
2yj−1+xi−1
e
5yj−3xi+20
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The upper Riemann sum is given by U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nMijΔxiΔyj where Mij is the maximum value of f in each subregion Rij.

We consider an arbitrary subregion Rij of the partition. This subregion lies between xi−1 and xi over the x-axis and yi−1 and yi over the y-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • f(x,y)=5y−3x+20 decreases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=5y−3x+20 increases as y increases.

As a result, the maximum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the largest possible y. This is the value at the top left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

Mij=f(xi−1,yj)=5yj−3xi−1+20 for all 1≤i≤m and 1≤j≤n.

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(5yj−3xi−1+20)ΔxiΔyj.

So, the missing expression is 5yj−3xi−1+20.
